progressive web app, a website that can be installed and behave like an app

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Browser marker and imports
sections.what: Marks the file as browser code and brings in the effect tool.
sections.why: Likely reason: service workers exist only in the browser.
sections.watch_out: Keep the browser marker so the code runs in the right place.

sections.name: PWARegister
sections.title: Service worker registration
sections.what: Runs once after the page loads, registers /sw.js if the browser supports it, and logs the outcome. Draws nothing.
sections.why: Likely reason: the helper must be registered once per visit.
sections.watch_out: The empty dependency list means it runs once per page load, so moving it into a loop would register it repeatedly.

summary: A component with no visible output that registers the site's service worker, which lets the site work like an installable app.
purpose: Lets the browser set up the helper script that can enable offline use and installation.
why: Likely reason: the progressive web app setup needs a registered service worker. The file's own comment says it has no interface.
how: 1. On page load in the browser, checks whether service workers are supported. 2. Registers the file at /sw.js. 3. Logs success with the scope, or a warning if registration fails.
inputs: The browser and the file at /sw.js.
risks: A failed registration only writes a warning, so the visitor gets no sign that offline or install support is missing.
debug: Look for the PWA messages in the browser console. If registration fails, confirm that /sw.js exists and is served over a secure connection.
